description: Use this when the user asks what a brand wants from a clip or what the rules are: short items in our words for format and length, must include (tags, disclosure, logo, sound, call to action), what to avoid, footage, social apps, language, audience countries, account rules and the deadline. Also the Brief Quality grade (A to F) and its red flag tags, how to join (open or application, minimum views, cap, platform fee, payout window), the before-you-post checklist and the link to the original brief. Also every rule grouped as the campaign page shows it: what to make, the full DO and DON'T lists, the caption (mentions and hashtags per app, the exact text, keywords, the bio link, the pinned comment), the FTC disclosure, brand safety, the audience (who, where from, how it is checked), page criteria (new or established pages, dedicated page, banned niches), posting rules, the creator profile, other requirements, the thresholds and caps (min views, min engagement, followers, max a creator, posts an account), each with its source (Platform, Brief, or Seen on slide 3), and the materials: the brief documents by name, the sound with its link and the example post URLs. Signed in, the brief documents include the files the clipping platform gives the clippers who join. Never a transcript or a media file. Read only.

campaign.description: The campaign as brand/series (for example lovable/clipping), its clippingalpha.com page URL, or its numeric campaignId from another tool.
